comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income for 2024 was $8.06 billion, representing a 27% increase from 2023, driven by higher interest income from trading assets, investments, and collateralized agreements due to higher balances and rates, partially offset by a decrease in deposits with banks.

sentences.text: Net interest income decreased $1.4 billion to $13.2 billion primarily due to higher deposit costs and lower average loan balances, partially offset by the benefit of higher average deposit balances.

Net interest income in the consolidated statements of earnings was $8.06 billion for 2024, 27% higher than 2023, reflecting an increase in interest income, partially offset by an increase in interest expense.

The increase in interest income primarily related to trading assets and investments (each reflecting the impact of higher average balances and higher average interest rates), collateralized agreements and other interest-earning assets (each reflecting the impact of higher average interest rates), partially offset by a decrease in interest income related to deposits with banks (reflecting the impact of lower average balances).

comparisons.peer_summary: Net interest income increased, driven by balance sheet actions including reinvestments in investment securities, higher revolving card balances, the timing impact of First Republic, higher wholesale deposit balances, and higher Markets net interest income, largely offset by deposit margin compression and lower average deposit balances in CCB.
comparisons.comparison: BAC reported a net interest income decrease primarily due to higher deposit costs and lower average loan balances. In contrast, JPM reported an increase in net interest income driven by balance sheet actions such as reinvestments in investment securities and higher revolving card balances, although JPM also noted that these gains were largely offset by deposit margin compression and lower average deposit balances in CCB. Both companies identified deposit margin compression/costs and loan/deposit balance dynamics as key factors, but with opposing net results (decrease for BAC vs. increase for JPM).

comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Net Interest Revenue Performance and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Wealth Management net interest revenues decreased 10% year-over-year to $7,313 million in 2024, primarily driven by lower average sweep deposits, partially offset by higher investment portfolio yields and lending growth.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS reported a decrease in their respective net interest income/net interest revenues for 2024. BAC attributed its decrease to higher deposit costs and lower average loan balances, while MS attributed its 10% decrease to lower average sweep deposits, partially offset by higher investment portfolio yields. Both companies faced headwinds from deposit-related factors (costs for BAC, volume/sweep deposits for MS) despite BAC's mention of lower loan balances versus MS's mention of lending growth offsets.
